content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
Entire Brain's supervised watch daemon (`entire-brain workspace watch --distill`, launchd unit `io.entire.brain-watch.*`, log at `~/.local/state/entire/logs/watch.log`) is the only automatic path that runs fact distillation: each 5-minute tick runs `runRefresh` in-process (internal/cli/watch.go around line 721) and, when refresh succeeds and the 24h `--distill-every` gate allows, `runDistill` (around line 799). On Karthik's machine the log shows 724 ticks over 20 days; 576 of them logged `[watch] refresh failed (skipping agent work this tick): brain_locked: timed out acquiring lock at .../locks/write.lock (held by pid N for 10s-25s)`, with a few holds of 11-16 minutes. Lock holders were many distinct short-lived pids, most likely memory-worker passes or session-end hook exports. Because any refresh failure skips the whole tick's agent work, the gated distill ran only 3 times in 20 days. A separate PR (#440, fix/distill-cache-salt-agent-independent) fixes an unrelated cache-salt bug; do not touch that. Also seen: `refresh: seed baseline failed` on 652 ticks and 91 `dirty_worktree` refusals, which may be the same root cause or separate.

Task:
Find out why the watch daemon's per-tick refresh times out on `locks/write.lock` so often, and make the tick resilient so lock contention does not starve the gated distill.

Start with `entire brain brief` and `entire brain recall` on the lock design (write.lock, manifest.lock, memory-worker.lock, lock timeouts) and `entire graph impact` on the lock helpers before editing. Read `internal/cli/watch.go` (tick loop, `runRefreshDeltaStats`, the refresh-then-distill ordering), the lock acquisition helpers (grep `withBrainWriteLock`, `file lock timeout`, `brain_locked`), and the memory worker launch path (`internal/cli/memory_cmd.go`, `memory_coordinator.go`) to see who holds write.lock for 10-25s per pass and what the daemon's acquisition timeout is.

Deliverables: (1) a short root-cause note in the PR description with the holder and the timeout numbers; (2) a fix such that a transient lock hold does not cancel the tick's agent work, for example a bounded retry/backoff on the tick's refresh, a longer daemon-side timeout, or running the gated distill when the previous refresh was recent enough even if this tick's refresh lost the lock, with the reasoning recorded; (3) tests in the watch test files covering a tick that meets a briefly held lock; (4) `go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'Watch'` green. Keep the change in watch and lock code; do not modify the distill cache salt code. Open a PR against main.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/krk/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_a7e73af0-9f5d-4e4f-a9ef-0e217b5087ac
I'll start by checking Brain/Graph availability, running the brief and recall on the lock design, then reading the watch tick loop and lock helpers.

# Watch daemon write.lock contention: root cause and fix (session inspiring-wright-68270a)

## Root cause (verified)
- `brainWriteLockTimeout` is 10s (internal/cli/brain.go:33), shared by every `withBrainWriteLock` caller (375 per `entire graph impact`), including interactive commands.
- Each tick runs: delta -> reconcile -> refresh. `reconcileMemoryAndLaunch` (memory_cmd.go) spawns a detached `entire-brain memory worker --once`. That worker's prepass (`runRefreshDeltaStats` with export: runExport + buildHistoryShortTermLockedContext, both under write.lock) and projection publish hold write.lock for 12-25s on this brain (a full pass is ~2m20s per history/work/v1/worker.log).
- The refresh asks for write.lock seconds later (session export, then seed baseline) and loses both 10s waits. The watch log says "held by pid N for 12s..25s" because the hold was already that old when the waiter gave up.
- Proof of holder identity: locks/write.lock.owner and locks/memory-worker.lock.owner both named pid 57068 (worker started 10:07:23Z, write.lock stamped 10:09:39Z). The watch's own delta step, which runs BEFORE the launch, succeeded on 686 of 724 ticks; the refresh, which runs AFTER the launch, failed on 576.
- Why every tick: the delta reports "14 transcripts failed to scan" on 652 ticks, so every tick is a "repair" tick: reconcile fires (worker launched) and the heavy refresh runs every tick (the repair backoff counter only advances on a SUCCESSFUL refresh, so it never backs off while the refresh keeps losing).
- "seed baseline failed" (652) is the same lock timeout inside the seed stage. "dirty_worktree" (91) is expected behaviour while the tree has uncommitted edits (issue #327) and the tick continues past it.
- The 21 long holds (15m37s, 1m4s) are a different holder (likely a distill pass or backfill); the retry does not cover them, the pending-work fallback does.

## Fix (internal/cli/watch.go only)
1. Worker launch (reconcile) moved AFTER the refresh outcome via a deferred closure with a ran-guard (same pattern as runFactsSync). Still runs once on every exit path.
2. `watchRefreshWithLockRetry`: refresh retried up to 3 times on lock-timeout errors only (errFileLockTimeout or "brain_locked:"), waits 15s/30s/60s, capped at --interval, ctx-aware; injectable `steps.sleep`.
3. `watchPendingAgentWorkUsable`: if every attempt loses, pending distill/seed set by an earlier successful refresh (within one --distill-every window) still runs; reserve is called with the cursor's own fingerprint so the refresh cursor is not advanced.
The 10s global timeout was deliberately not changed.

## Follow-ups (not done here)
- Why 14 transcripts fail to scan every tick (makes every tick a repair tick and launches a worker per tick).
- Memory worker holds write.lock across the whole short-term build in its prepass; shortening that hold would reduce contention for everyone (hooks, MCP, brief).
EOF

Stop the watch tick losing write.lock to the worker it just launched

The supervised watch daemon lost locks/write.lock on 576 of 724 ticks over
20 days on one machine, and because a failed refresh skips the tick's agent
work, the 24h-gated distill ran three times in those 20 days.

Root cause: each tick ran delta -> reconcile -> refresh. The reconcile step
spawns a detached `memory worker --once`, whose prepass export and
projection publish hold the brain write lock for 12-25s on a real brain.
The heavy refresh asked for the same lock a second or two later with the
10s brainWriteLockTimeout, lost it in the session export and again in the
seed baseline, and aborted the tick. The lock owner sidecars named the
same pid for write.lock and memory-worker.lock, and the delta step, which
runs before the launch, succeeded on 686 of those ticks.

Three changes, all in watch.go:

- The reconcile (worker launch) now runs after the refresh outcome, as a
  deferred closure with a ran-guard like runFactsSync, so the tick never
  races its own child. It still runs once on every exit path.
- The free refresh is retried on lock-timeout errors only, up to three
  times with 15s/30s/60s waits capped at --interval and cancelled by ctx.
  The 10s global timeout is left alone: it is shared by hundreds of
  callers including interactive commands.
- When every attempt loses, pending distill/seed set by an earlier
  successful refresh within one --distill-every window still runs, with
  the refresh cursor left where it was so the next tick retries. This is
  the same rule the no-change path already applies.

EOF
